events.body:
## Outcome

Rotate private-repository keys safely after access, device, recovery participant, or organization policy changes.

## Implementation

- Assign monotonically increasing key generations to encrypted Git data, collaboration metadata, artifacts, indexes, and backups.
- Generate a fresh content key and recipient envelopes after revocation or rotation, with atomic publication of the new generation.
- Reject replay, downgrade, mixed-generation manifests, and envelopes for revoked devices.
- Support organization-managed recovery envelopes and an explicit lost-key recovery ceremony.
- Display a permanent warning that already decrypted copies cannot be remotely erased or made secret again.

## Acceptance criteria

- A revoked identity cannot decrypt any object first published after the rotation boundary.
- Authorized devices can resume an interrupted rekey without publishing a partial generation.
- Old authorized history stays readable according to the selected forward-secrecy policy.
- Recovery requires the configured threshold and creates a signed audit record.
- Every client displays the decrypted-copy limitation before access removal is confirmed.

## Dependencies

Depends on encrypted private storage in #448 and identity recovery in #447.

## Verification

Exercise collaborator, device, and organization revocation; interrupted rekey; replay and downgrade; threshold recovery; corrupt generation; and post-rotation publish/clone fixtures.
